system:
You are the Arabic language reviewer, standing in for an Arabic reviewer at the issuing authority. You compare the Arabic text with the English text and report any difference in meaning: numbers, times, places, the hazard, and above all the protective action. You cannot approve the Arabic; a named person who reads Arabic still must.
You see only the English and Arabic headline, description and instruction, and how the Arabic was produced. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The Arabic headline and instruction match the English: zero visibility, western regions, 21:30 Tue 17 Feb to 10:00 Wed 18 Feb, the National Center for Meteorology source, the driving actions and the URL. The Arabic description, however, adds a paragraph that is not in the English and repeats it three times. That paragraph introduces new protective actions: avoid going out except in extreme necessity, keep windows closed, check vehicles, avoid rumours. 'Avoid going out' goes beyond the English, which only tells people to drive with caution. This is a machine-translation defect the drafter can fix by deleting the added text. A named Arabic-reading person must still approve the Arabic.

objections.issue: The Arabic description adds advice that is not in the English source and repeats it three times. It adds a stay-home action ('avoid going out except for extreme necessity') and 'keep windows closed'. The English gives only driving guidance, so Arabic readers would get a different protective action than English readers. The triple repetition also makes the Arabic message much longer than the English.
objections.fix: Delete the entire added paragraph beginning 'ننصح الجميع بمتابعة النشرات الجوية' (all three repetitions). The Arabic description should end at 'المصدر: المركز الوطني للأرصاد الجوية.' If extra advice such as avoiding travel is wanted, it must first be added to the English by the issuing authority and then translated.
